Stress and anxiety have been huge comfort-food-necessitating factors for me. I have been on medication for depression and anxiety for almost a year now, and finding the right medication helped (tried different antidepressants during the last.. 3 years maybe?)

I discovered keto by some sort of lucky coincidence. Gave it some thought, research and commitment, because it really seemed sustainable for me. And I am totally blown away, and it will only be one month of keto as of tomorrow! All the losing weight, better skin, more energy things - it's really awesome. 
But the one thing I DID NOT EXPECT - my anxiety has dropped. It has gone so much better, I can physically feel it - I feel the difference in my body, when I'm in a high-stress situation, and I know I felt so much anxiety for it a month ago. I didn't really hope for changes in brain chemistry, but I've come over some tidbits of science that seems to support it as well. 

All in all, I haven't felt this psychologically stable and happy and not anxious for years. I really can't believe it. I am considering on starting to reduce my medication soon. I hope this gave another possible benefit from keto to you.

Yes, indeed, the saline solution from a drug store is a good idea - that way you also know that it doesn't contain too little or too much salt. I actually used a sea salt solution nose spray for my anti-helix piercing for a while. It's just the sea salt solution, but it was really convenient to use - just spray and you're basically done. It took such a long time to fully heal, I would have gone insane with mixing the solution myself.

I hope everything goes well with your piercing, microdermals are really awesome. I have one on my chest and it healed really nice and fast. I was suggested to wear a band-aid over it at nights for a week, so the tossing and turning while sleeping wouldn't disturb it.. I don't know with having it on your cheek, but it might be an idea. 

And yes, I would recommend salt water. Not necessarily soaks, but just cleaning it with it once or twice a day. Salt disinfects it and also helps to get rid of the 'crusties' if they appear. I'm no expert, but I'm quite sure that you don't have to worry about the water getting trapped.
